title: Completed and audited the six-state V7 footprint product
summary: Production and full source-identity coverage checks completed for Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Colorado and Connecticut: 25,092,517 buildings, including 913,169 with footprint modifications (about 3.64%).
note: This is a production-completeness result, not a new geometry-accuracy evaluation or a claim that the complete package has been uploaded. The frozen production model and scientific rules were unchanged.
details: Of 25,092,558 unique source IDs, all valid sources were accounted for with zero missing valid IDs and zero extra IDs. The remaining 41 records are verified invalid original geometries and remain explicitly quarantined. Counts by state: AL 2,846,169; AR 1,759,917; AZ 3,071,363; CA 13,243,143; CO 2,564,259; CT 1,607,666. Completion was recorded at 04:25 EDT on October 22.

title: Resumed regional production beyond the completed six states
summary: A separate regional generation continued toward the contiguous United States and DC, reusing completed six-state results. The October 22, 14:38 EDT snapshot recorded 31,814 additional buildings and 2,146 modifications around the Delaware–Maryland area.
note: These are dated progress counts, not a live monitor or a completed regional or national release. The current region still had 9,112 buildings outstanding at that snapshot.
details: The workflow retains complete input context across administrative boundaries, deduplicates shared grids, and separates processing context from delivery geography. Production and export/upload run independently; checkpoint continuation was scheduled, but scheduling alone does not establish successful continuation.

title: Defined complete regional replacement for incremental releases
summary: An accepted region will replace all older current-product records in that region with its complete new output, including unchanged buildings. Older data outside the accepted region remains in the current product.
note: The October 22 handoff recorded the complete six-state package in export and verification preparation; successful public upload of that package was not yet verified. The public repository link is not proof of this new release.

sources.label: Public data repository (check its current manifest)

details: Different old/new building counts are allowed. Region membership follows fixed original ownership, and whole footprints are retained. Missing inputs or failed work cannot be treated as an accepted empty region. The first replacement covers the six completed states; the other 42 states plus DC retain their existing data.

title: Completed a matched image-line refinement and DL comparison
summary: Compared an adaptation of Jung & Sohn (2019) with the existing DL-assisted local roof reassignment on eight Georgetown buildings under two shared-input settings. All 16 pairs share observations, footprints and the same initial Roofer model; the paper adaptation ran 48 optimization trials across three seeds.
note: This implements the paper’s core ideas with declared substitutions, not the original algorithm in full. Independent target roof ground truth is absent, so no real-world accuracy winner is established.
details: The adaptation uses NAIP line/corner cues, contour proposals, fitting and complexity terms, and annealed search while holding roof planes fixed. Twelve analytic cases showed aggregate improvement for boundary shifts but inconsistent orientation/corner behavior. Clean-package replay exactly reproduced one changed candidate from each method. Unchanged models and rejected candidates remain visible.

title: Tested local bumps, depressions and roof-plane reassignment
summary: A bounded validation reused frozen point-model scores on eight real buildings and tested 48 analytic cases. Two real local-replacement candidates were proposed; only one passed the fixed shell-edge diagnostic.
note: This is not a newly trained correction network. OSM 67521425 remains unresolved: its proposed changed candidate failed the edge check, and the checked export retains the preceding model. Geometric validity does not establish roof accuracy.

sources.label: Local repair methods, cases and models

details: The final validation preserves original XYZ and point indices and labels reassigned surfaces as generated geometry. Coherent planar contamination and total occlusion remain unresolved; low support alone does not justify flattening or filling a roof. Earlier invalid development probes were superseded by the corrected final run.

title: Compared fusion order and guarded canopy filtering
summary: Compared the original joint filtering workflow, point-cloud-first reconstruction, and strong point evidence with observed-plane protection on the same eight buildings. In two inspected cases, the guarded method removed 150 and 16 candidate points, compared with 10 and 6 in the original workflow.
note: Removed-point counts are not tree-classification accuracy. Lower model peaks do not prove a more accurate roof; both remaining canopy and mistakenly removed roof support require independent checks.

sources.label: Three methods, point decisions and roof models

details: The original fusion rule screened out only 136 of 21,383 candidates. Most suspected residual canopy points never reached the fusion threshold. The revised method allows strong point evidence to act despite optical conflict and protects points near supported planes. No new network was trained for this comparison.

title: Connected real inputs to an eight-building LoD2 workflow
summary: Connected NAIP imagery, original 3DEP points and footprints through conservative point filtering, Roofer reconstruction, semantic roof-support review, shell diagnostics and export. All eight cases produced native LoD2 outputs.
note: The first version removed 136 points at the front end but triggered no additional backend trimming. Initial and final models were therefore identical; this verifies execution, not backend effectiveness or improved accuracy.
details: Six roof surfaces with insufficient observed support were retained for review. Fully occluded roof completion is not implemented. The experiment keeps original point decisions, input provenance, failures and fallback records.

title: Expanded training and evaluated roof-support filtering across cities
summary: Completed 26 training runs across 16 configurations, with up to 20,000 training buildings. Evaluation covered 200 buildings in Groningen and Maastricht, 12 simulated observation conditions and 19 reconstruction workflows.
note: These results use automatic 3DBAG teacher roofs and simulated point observations. They do not establish accuracy on real AHN/3DEP data or US roofs. RGB imagery is for inspection, not an input to the newly trained point models.

sources.label: Controlled results and full experiment archive

details: The source-validation-selected local model reduced the mean penalized roof loss from 1.0940 to 0.5123 m. The loss includes failure and missing-coverage penalties; it is not successful-roof MAE. Extra gains from larger training sets and longer training were not clearly established. Real-point diagnostics still showed the risk of removing roof-support points.

title: Tested learned filtering and its clean-roof tradeoff
summary: A first cross-city study used 500 training, 160 validation and 160 test buildings from 3DBAG. A fixed 24-building subset underwent 720 roof reconstruction comparisons. Learned filtering reduced dense simulated canopy error but also damaged clean roofs.
note: The controlled experiments use simulated observations. A separate Boston probe on 18 real buildings and 47,544 candidates did not establish a reconstruction-success improvement or independently verified roof accuracy.
details: For dense simulated canopy, mean vertical error was 2.14 m for raw points, 1.27 m after PointNet filtering and 1.49 m with a local model plus roof protection. On clean roofs the corresponding values were 0.40, 0.55 and 0.52 m. Point-classification quality alone did not determine reconstruction quality.

title: Expanded the input-quality comparison to 120 buildings
summary: Extended the Georgetown comparison to the original 60 buildings plus 60 additional cases, testing 12 configurations. Local registration and aggressive simplification did not provide consistent benefits across the two groups.
note: Metrics use held-out observations from the same point-cloud acquisition, not independent roof ground truth. Improvements on the original cases did not consistently transfer to the additional cases.
details: Published the initial three experiment chapters together with actual model geometry, candidate/held-out point membership, imagery and per-building inspection. The current archive preserves those historical results.

title: Separated registration and point filtering in a four-way comparison
summary: Compared raw input, registration alone, point filtering alone and their combination on 60 fixed buildings. Combined preprocessing changed common-point mean absolute error from 0.6546 to 0.6513 m, while coverage fell from 99.69% to 93.83%.
note: The small common-point error reduction does not establish an overall quality gain. These are same-acquisition held-out observations, and the registration groups each included a candidate that failed the fixed edge diagnostic.
details: The global footprint translation was 0.25 m west and 1.00 m north; filtering removed 3.65% of candidate points. NAIP did not participate in this preprocessing reconstruction experiment. Original crop membership was fixed, so recovering newly available points after registration remained untested.

title: Established five reconstruction baselines in Georgetown
summary: Built a 60-building pilot using 2014 NAIP imagery, 2014 3DEP points and USBF footprints. Compared native Roofer, LiDAR roof templates, image-oriented templates, free-plane reconstruction and image-assisted plane partitioning.
note: The best held-out fit in this pilot was Roofer at 0.743 m MAE. Evaluation used a fixed 20% holdout from the same LiDAR acquisition, not independent ground truth. No new deep-learning model was trained in this round.
details: Simple optical orientation cues provided limited gains, and none of the tested alternatives surpassed Roofer on this metric. This motivated closer inspection of registration, contamination, roof support and topology.

title: Audited reference data before treating city models as roof truth
summary: Reviewed the distinction between footprint-and-height extrusion and roof-structure reconstruction, and audited potential LoD2 reference sources. The research direction narrowed toward using real observations to adapt roof reconstruction across regions.
note: Automatically reconstructed city models and building-energy models are not automatically independent roof ground truth. Pairing, acquisition time, registration, roof detail and fallback geometry need to be checked separately.
details: The planned evaluation separates point support, plane/ridge structure, coverage, reconstruction failure and shell validity. These are research requirements, not evidence that the proposed method is already accurate.

title: Rebased manuscript review on the author-reviewed draft
summary: The manuscript discussion identified the author-reviewed USBF draft as the baseline for further sentence-level review and emphasized describing specific footprint-editing scenarios rather than broadly claiming improved accuracy.
note: This records a manuscript-review decision, not submission, acceptance or confirmation that every suggested edit was incorporated. Selected visual changes do not override aggregate evaluation results.

title: Reviewed the current footprint production and recovery checkpoint
summary: The latest project handoff recorded substantial progress in the building-footprint production workflow and a completed producer segment that committed new buildings. Work to recover storage capacity and resume the next production segment was still in progress.
note: This describes the October 16 project snapshot, not a verified live status or a completed nationwide release. A proposed million-file recovery target had not been certified.

title: Verified new buildings from a regional production run
summary: A bounded regional run ended cleanly, reporting 14,876 newly committed buildings and 779 footprint modifications. A separate trial showed that a larger input catalog could produce and verify another nonempty building batch.
note: These are regional and trial results, not a nationwide completion count. A two-host computing pilot remained separate from the canonical production workflow.

title: Tested an indexed input archive for footprint processing
summary: Independent component checks and bounded real-data comparisons showed that archived inputs could be read while preserving the tested building geometry and output attributes.
note: These checks did not establish nationwide throughput or authorize removal of the original inputs.

title: Prepared a highlighted manuscript and sentence-level review
summary: Prepared a highlighted revision of the manuscript and supplementary methods, checked citation numbering, and created a separate sentence-level review with optional tracked English suggestions.
note: The suggested edits are separate from the highlighted revision. Structural checks passed, but desktop Word rendering and independent validation of footprint changes were not completed.

title: Completed a guarded footprint-input cleanup batch
summary: A verified cleanup batch removed eligible intermediate pixel files after checking product identities, input dependencies and recoverability. The work freed storage capacity for continued footprint production.
note: The remaining storage constraint was not resolved by this batch, and the removed files were a bounded eligible cohort rather than the full input collection.

title: Prepared tracked revisions to the manuscript and methods
summary: Prepared Word tracked-change versions of the main manuscript and supplementary methods. The revision clarified the distinction between national counts and regional evaluation, refined method descriptions, and updated figures and cross-references.
note: The shared source manuscript was not overwritten. Independent evidence that every modified footprint improved remains an open research question; this entry does not indicate submission or acceptance.

title: Compared footprint pipeline revisions on matched inputs
summary: Repeated isolated comparisons found matching building attributes, geometry, ownership and candidate records between the existing and revised workflows. The revision reduced elapsed time in these tests, but missed its planned speedup targets.
note: The measured gains came from isolated test cohorts. Sustained improvement in live production had not been established.

title: Completed controlled NAIP footprint-model training studies
summary: Across October 2-4, several matched training comparisons explored model structure, quality retention and residual learning for aerial-image building footprints. The inspected run logs show the training and validation stages completed.
note: The inspected logs do not establish which candidate improved held-out footprint accuracy.

title: Verified a single-building energy-model run
summary: An AutoBEM/OpenStudio example generated a building model, simulation inputs and time-series electricity output, and its run report marked the example successful.
note: This verifies one building example; batch modeling and validation against observed energy use remain to be demonstrated.

title: Revised the manuscript's building-product section
summary: Prepared tracked revisions to the building-product section, checked national counts and regional evaluation results, and refined the corresponding descriptions.
note: This entry does not indicate paper submission.

title: Measured early footprint-pipeline changes in isolated replays
summary: Small replay cohorts showed faster processing while preserving the checked final building geometry. A grouped scheduling approach did not reproduce its short-test gain in live production and was rolled back.
note: The replay measurements do not establish a sustained national production speedup. Candidate screening remained experimental.
